cuisines.name: Gujarati
states: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

ingredients: 500 g rohu or katla steaks, rubbed with 1/2 tsp turmeric and salt
1 small brinjal or 100 g potol, cut in batons
1 tsp ginger paste, 1 tsp cumin powder
1/2 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder
steps: Heat mustard oil until it smokes lightly, then fry the fish 2 minutes a side over medium-high heat until golden; set aside.
In the same oil fry the potatoes and brinjal until lightly browned at the edges.
Add kalo jeere and green chillies, then the ginger, cumin, turmeric and chilli mixed with a little water; fry 2 minutes until the oil separates.
Pour in 2 cups water with salt and simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 12 minutes.
Slip in the fried fish and simmer 5 minutes; scatter coriander and serve the thin jhol with plain rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 6 hilsa (ilish) steaks, rubbed with turmeric and salt
3 tbsp black and yellow mustard seeds, soaked 20 minutes
steps: Grind the soaked mustard seeds with 2 green chillies, a pinch of salt and a little water into a smooth paste (do not over-grind or it turns bitter).
Heat mustard oil to smoking, lightly fry the ilish 1 minute a side and remove.
Temper kalo jeere and slit chillies in the oil, add the mustard paste, turmeric and 1 cup water, and bring to a gentle boil.
Return the fish, cover and simmer 6–8 minutes on low heat until cooked through; finish with a raw drizzle of mustard oil and serve with hot rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 tbsp mustard paste (black and yellow sorshe)
2 tbsp grated coconut or poppy-seed paste (optional)
steps: Mix the mustard paste, coconut, yogurt, turmeric, salt and 3 tbsp mustard oil into a thick coating.
Toss the ilish in it and pack into a steel tiffin box; tuck in the chillies and drizzle the remaining oil.
Close the lid and steam in a pan of simmering water for 15–18 minutes until the flesh flakes.
Serve straight from the box with plain steamed rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g bhetki (barramundi) fillets, cut in 8 pieces
8 banana-leaf squares, softened over a flame
steps: Mix mustard paste, coconut, chilli paste, turmeric, salt and mustard oil; coat the fish and rest 15 minutes.
Place each piece with a chilli on a banana leaf, fold into a parcel and tie.
Cook the parcels on an oiled tawa covered with a lid on medium-low heat, 8–10 minutes per side, until the leaf chars and the fish is opaque.
Unwrap at the table and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g large prawns (golda chingri), cleaned, heads on
2 bay leaves, 2 cardamom, 2 cloves, 1 inch cinnamon
1/2 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder
steps: Rub prawns with turmeric and salt; fry in mustard oil 1 minute a side and remove.
Temper bay leaves and whole spices, then fry the onion and ginger on medium heat until light golden.
Add chilli powder, sugar and salt, then the coconut milk; simmer 5 minutes.
Return the prawns and cook 5–6 minutes until they curl and are opaque.
Finish with ghee and garam masala; serve with plain rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tbsp ginger paste, 1 tbsp garlic paste
2 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp cumin powder
2 bay leaves, 4 cardamom, 4 cloves, 1 inch cinnamon
1 tsp Bengali garam masala, 1 tbsp ghee, salt
steps: Marinate the mutton in yogurt, onion paste, ginger, garlic, turmeric, chilli and salt for 4 hours.
Heat mustard oil, caramelise sugar, add whole spices and sliced onions and fry until deep brown.
Add the mutton and kosha (sauté) on medium-low heat, stirring, for 40–50 minutes until dark and the oil separates.
Add potatoes and 1 cup hot water, cover and cook until the meat is tender, about 30 minutes (or 4 pressure-cooker whistles).
Finish with garam masala and ghee; serve the thick gravy with luchi or porota.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tbsp ginger paste, 1 tbsp garlic paste
6 dried red chillies, 2 bay leaves, 4 green cardamom, 1 tsp shahi jeera
1 tsp kewra water, a pinch of mace and nutmeg
steps: Marinate mutton in yogurt, onion paste, ginger, garlic and salt for 4 hours.
Heat ghee, temper whole spices and red chillies, then add the mutton with its marinade.
Cook covered on low heat for 60–75 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender.
Stir in cashew-posto paste, sugar, mace and nutmeg and simmer 10 minutes; the gravy should stay pale and creamy.
Sprinkle kewra water and serve with naan or Kolkata biryani.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg mutton, marinated overnight in yogurt, ginger-garlic, chilli and salt
3 cups aged basmati rice, soaked 30 minutes
1 tsp kewra water, 1 tsp rose water, a pinch of saffron in warm milk
Whole spices: bay leaves, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, mace
steps: Cook the marinated mutton with ghee, half the beresta and biryani masala, covered, until tender (about 60 minutes); keep the gravy short.
Fry the potatoes and eggs in ghee until golden.
Boil rice with whole spices and salt until 70% done; drain.
Layer rice, mutton, potatoes and eggs in a heavy pot; top with saffron milk, kewra, rose water, ghee and remaining onions.
Seal with a lid and dough and cook on dum over very low heat for 25–30 minutes; serve with mutton rezala or chicken chaap.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tbsp ginger paste, 1 tbsp garlic paste
2 tbsp poppy-seed paste, 2 tbsp cashew paste
1/2 tsp mace-nutmeg powder, 1 tsp kewra water
steps: Marinate chicken in yogurt, ginger, garlic, chilli, poppy and cashew pastes, sugar and salt for 4 hours.
Heat ghee in a wide pan and lay the chicken in flat.
Cook covered on very low heat for 40–50 minutes, turning once, until the gravy is thick and oil floats on top.
Sprinkle mace-nutmeg and kewra; serve with Kolkata biryani or roomali roti.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder
2 bay leaves, 2 cardamom, 2 cloves, 1 inch cinnamon
steps: Rub fish with turmeric and salt and fry in smoking mustard oil until golden; remove.
Temper whole spices and bay leaves, then fry onion and ginger paste until light brown.
Lower the heat, stir in yogurt mixed with chilli powder, sugar and salt, and cook 5 minutes stirring so it doesn't split.
Add 1/2 cup water and the fish; simmer 6–8 minutes and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tbsp ginger paste, 1 tsp garlic paste
1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli, 1 tsp cumin powder
2 bay leaves and whole garam masala
1 tsp ghee, 1/2 tsp garam masala powder
steps: Marinate the rui with turmeric and salt and fry in smoking mustard oil until crisp; set aside.
Temper bay leaves and whole spices, add onion paste and fry until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic, tomato, powdered spices, yogurt and sugar; kasha (sauté) until the oil separates.
Add 1 cup water, bring to a boil, add fish and simmer 8 minutes until the gravy is rich and thick.
Finish with ghee and garam masala; serve with rice for festive lunches.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp ginger paste, 1 tsp cumin paste
1 tsp turmeric, 2 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder
steps: Rub koi with turmeric and salt and fry in plenty of hot mustard oil until crisp; remove.
In the same oil temper kalo jeere and green chillies, add onion, ginger and cumin pastes and fry until the oil separates.
Add chilli powder, sugar, salt and 1/2 cup water; simmer 3 minutes.
Add the koi and cook 5–7 minutes until a thick, oily red gravy clings to the fish; serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Rub pabda with turmeric and salt and fry lightly in mustard oil (they are delicate, so turn once only).
Temper kalo jeere and chillies, add mustard paste, chilli powder and 1 cup water and bring to a boil.
Slide in the fish and simmer 6–8 minutes on low heat until cooked and the jhal is thickened.
Drizzle raw mustard oil, add coriander and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix mustard paste, coconut, yogurt, turmeric, salt, sugar and 2 tbsp mustard oil.
Coat the prawns and pack into a steel tiffin box; top with chillies and the remaining oil.
Close and steam over simmering water 12–15 minutes until the prawns are pink and firm.
Serve with hot rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 cup moong dal, dry-roasted until nutty
1 rohu fish head, cut in pieces, rubbed with turmeric and salt
2 bay leaves, 1 tsp whole cumin, 2 dried red chillies
steps: Boil the roasted dal with turmeric and 4 cups water until soft but holding shape, about 20 minutes.
Fry the fish head in smoking mustard oil until crisp and break it up roughly.
Temper cumin, bay leaves and red chillies, add ginger and cumin powder, then the fish head; fry 2 minutes.
Pour in the dal with salt and sugar and simmer 10 minutes; finish with ghee and garam masala and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g boneless chicken cubes, marinated in yogurt, ginger-garlic, chilli and salt for 2 hours
Paratha dough: 2 cups maida, 2 tbsp oil, salt, water
steps: Thread the chicken on skewers and grill or tawa-roast until charred and cooked through.
Roll the rested dough into thin parathas and cook on a hot tawa with oil until flaky.
Pour a beaten egg on the tawa, press the paratha on top and cook until the egg sets.
Line with chicken, onion, chillies, lime, chaat masala and sauces; roll tightly in paper and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Dough: 2 cups maida, 2 tbsp ghee, salt, water
Cucumber-onion salad and potato curry to serve
steps: Knead a soft dough with ghee and rest 30 minutes.
Stretch each ball into a very thin square on an oiled surface.
Beat eggs with onion, chillies, coriander, salt and pepper; spoon into the centre and fold the sheet into a parcel.
Shallow-fry in a hot tawa with oil, turning, until both sides are crisp and the egg is cooked; serve with salad and aloo curry.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g bhetki fillets, cut in flat ovals
2 tbsp onion paste, 2 green chillies ground with coriander
steps: Marinate fish in ginger-garlic, onion, chilli-coriander paste, lime, salt and pepper for 30 minutes.
Dip each piece in egg and press firmly into breadcrumbs; repeat for a double coat.
Deep-fry in medium-hot oil 4–5 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Serve with kasundi (mustard sauce) and onion-cucumber salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Ginger-garlic paste, green chilli-coriander paste, lime, salt
steps: Marinate the fish 30 minutes, then crumb it.
Deep-fry until golden and cooked through.
Beat eggs with cornflour and salt; drizzle the mixture in thin threads into hot oil and quickly wrap the lacy egg net around each fried fillet.
Fry until the net is crisp and golden; serve with kasundi.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 chicken breasts, butterflied and pounded thin
Green chilli paste, lime juice, pepper, salt
steps: Marinate the pounded chicken 30 minutes.
Dip in egg and press firmly into breadcrumbs, shaping into flat cutlets.
Deep-fry on medium heat 5–6 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Serve with kasundi and onion salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp ginger paste, 2 green chillies, chopped
1/2 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1/2 tsp garam masala
steps: Fry onion, ginger and chillies in oil, add mashed potato, spices and salt and cook until dry.
Wrap each egg half in the potato mixture, keeping an oval shape.
Dip in beaten egg, roll in breadcrumbs and deep-fry until golden.
Serve hot with kasundi or ketchup.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli, 1 tsp cumin powder
steps: Prick the eggs, rub with turmeric and salt and fry in mustard oil until blistered; fry the potatoes too.
Temper bay leaves and whole spices, add onion and ginger paste and fry until golden.
Add tomato, spices, sugar and salt and cook until the oil separates.
Add 1.5 cups water and potatoes, simmer until tender, then add eggs and cook 5 minutes; serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Rub ghee into flour and salt until it holds when pressed; knead into a smooth, firm dough with water and rest 20 minutes.
Divide into small balls and roll into thin 10 cm circles using a dab of oil (no dry flour).
Deep-fry one at a time in hot oil, pressing gently so they puff; remove while still pale white.
Serve with aloor dom, cholar dal or kosha mangsho.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp fennel, 1 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp hing
steps: Grind the soaked dal coarsely with ginger and chilli.
Fry the paste in ghee with roasted ground fennel and cumin, hing, salt and sugar until dry; cool.
Knead maida with ghee, salt and water; stuff each ball with the dal filling and roll gently.
Deep-fry until puffed and pale golden; serve with aloor dom or cholar dal.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Grind peas coarsely with ginger and chillies without water.
Fry the paste in a little oil with hing, roasted spices, sugar and salt until dry; cool.
Knead maida with ghee, salt and water; rest 20 minutes, stuff with the pea filling and roll gently.
Deep-fry until puffed and pale green-gold; serve with aloor dom.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g baby potatoes, boiled and peeled
1 tsp cumin powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli
2 bay leaves, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 2 dried red chillies
3 tbsp mustard oil, 1 tsp ghee, 1/2 tsp garam masala
steps: Prick the potatoes and fry with turmeric in mustard oil until golden.
Temper bay leaves, cumin and red chillies, add ginger and tomato and cook until thick.
Add powdered spices, yogurt, sugar and salt and cook until the oil separates.
Add potatoes and 1/2 cup water and simmer 10 minutes to a thick coating gravy; finish with ghee and garam masala and serve with luchi.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1/4 cup coconut, cut in small slices
2 bay leaves, 1 tsp cumin, 2 dried red chillies
steps: Boil dal with turmeric and salt until soft but whole (2 whistles).
Fry coconut slices in ghee until golden; set aside.
Temper bay leaves, cumin, red chillies and whole spices, add ginger, then pour in the dal.
Add sugar, raisins and coconut and simmer 10 minutes; serve with luchi or kochuri.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 raw banana, 1 sweet potato, 1 brinjal, 2 drumsticks, 100 g ridge gourd, cut in batons
1 tbsp mustard paste, 1 tsp ginger paste
steps: Fry bori and bitter gourd in mustard oil until golden; set aside.
Temper radhuni, add the remaining vegetables and sauté 5 minutes.
Add ginger, mustard paste, salt and 1 cup water; cover and cook until tender.
Add milk, sugar, bitter gourd and crushed bori; simmer 5 minutes.
Finish with ghee and a sprinkle of roasted panch phoron powder; serve as the first course with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 tbsp poppy seeds (posto), soaked and ground
steps: Temper kalo jeere and chillies in mustard oil.
Add potatoes, turmeric and salt; cover and cook until almost tender.
Stir in the posto paste and a splash of water and cook until it coats the potatoes and turns dry.
Drizzle raw mustard oil and serve with rice and dal.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 large round brinjal, sliced 1 cm thick
steps: Rub the brinjal slices with turmeric, chilli, sugar and salt; rest 10 minutes.
Shallow-fry in hot mustard oil on medium heat, 4 minutes a side, until soft and golden.
Serve with khichuri or rice and dal.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g leafy greens (lal shak, palong or pui shak), chopped
steps: Temper kalo jeere and red chillies in mustard oil.
Add brinjal and fry until soft.
Add greens, salt and sugar and stir-fry on high heat until wilted and dry; serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg mixed vegetables: pumpkin, radish, potato, sweet potato, brinjal, beans, cauliflower, spinach stems
steps: Temper panch phoron, bay leaves and red chillies in mustard oil.
Add the hard vegetables first, then the soft ones, with ginger, turmeric, cumin and salt.
Cover and cook on low heat until soft and partly mashed.
Add sugar and ghee; serve with bhoger khichuri.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g mixed vegetables: potato, pumpkin, brinjal, radish, beans, cut in batons
steps: Temper panch phoron and chillies in mustard oil.
Add vegetables, turmeric and salt; cover and cook on low heat until tender.
Add mustard paste and sugar and cook uncovered until dry and slightly caught at the bottom; serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 cup chana dal, soaked overnight and ground coarse
1 tsp cumin powder, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli
Mustard oil, 1 tbsp ghee, 1/2 tsp garam masala
steps: Cook the dal paste with hing, ginger, chillies and salt in a little oil until it leaves the pan; spread on a plate, cool and cut into diamonds (dhoka).
Shallow-fry the dhoka until golden.
Temper bay leaves and cumin, fry potatoes, then add tomato and powdered spices and cook until the oil separates.
Add 1.5 cups water and simmer until the potatoes are done; add dhoka, simmer 3 minutes, and finish with ghee and garam masala.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 banana flower (mocha), cleaned and chopped, boiled with turmeric and salt
2 tbsp mustard oil, 1 tbsp ghee, 1/2 tsp garam masala
steps: Squeeze the boiled mocha dry.
Temper cumin and bay leaves in mustard oil and fry the potato until golden.
Add mocha, ginger, cumin powder, turmeric, sugar and salt; cook 10 minutes, stirring.
Add coconut and cook until dry; finish with ghee and garam masala.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g raw jackfruit (echor), peeled and cubed
1 tsp cumin powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp chilli
steps: Boil the jackfruit with turmeric and salt until just tender (oil your hands and knife when cutting).
Fry jackfruit and potatoes in mustard oil until golden.
Temper bay leaves and whole spices, add ginger, tomato and powdered spices and cook until the oil separates.
Add vegetables, sugar and 1 cup water and simmer until thick; finish with ghee and garam masala.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Filling: 100 g paneer (chhana), 2 tbsp raisins, 2 tbsp cashews, 1/2 tsp garam masala, salt, sugar
1 onion-free gravy base: 2 tomatoes puréed, 1 tsp ginger paste
1 tsp cumin powder, 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli, 1/2 tsp turmeric
steps: Fry the hollowed potol in mustard oil until blistered.
Cook the chhana with raisins, cashews, garam masala, salt and sugar until dry; stuff the potol.
Temper bay leaves, add ginger, tomato, spices, yogurt and cashew paste and cook until the oil separates.
Add 1 cup water and the stuffed potol; simmer 10 minutes and finish with ghee.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 bottle gourd (lau), peeled and finely diced
steps: Temper cumin and bay leaves in mustard oil, add ginger and lau with turmeric and salt.
Cover and cook on low heat until the lau releases water and softens, about 15 minutes.
Add milk, sugar and crushed bori and cook until almost dry.
Finish with ghee and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 cup moong dal, dry-roasted until golden and nutty
1 tsp cumin seeds, 2 bay leaves, 2 dried red chillies
1/4 cup green peas or cubed cauliflower (optional)
steps: Wash the roasted dal and boil with turmeric and 4 cups water until soft, about 20 minutes.
Temper cumin, bay leaves and red chillies in oil and ghee, add ginger and vegetables and fry 2 minutes.
Pour in the dal with salt and sugar and simmer 10 minutes; serve with rice and begun bhaja.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Boil the dal with turmeric and 4 cups water until completely soft; whisk smooth.
Temper kalo jeere, chillies and onion in mustard oil until the onion is golden.
Pour the tempering into the dal with salt and simmer 5 minutes; serve thin with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 cauliflower, florets; 2 potatoes, cubed; 1/2 cup peas
2 bay leaves, 1 tsp cumin, 2 dried red chillies, whole garam masala
steps: Wash the rice and dal; boil dal with turmeric in 6 cups water for 10 minutes.
Fry cauliflower and potatoes in ghee; temper bay leaves, cumin, red chillies and whole spices with ginger.
Add rice, dal, vegetables, cumin powder, salt and sugar; simmer stirring until soft and porridge-like, about 25 minutes.
Add peas and a final spoon of ghee; serve with labra, begun bhaja and chutney as bhog.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 cups gobindobhog rice, washed and drained 30 minutes
2 bay leaves, 4 cardamom, 4 cloves, 1 inch cinnamon
steps: Rub the rice with turmeric and salt.
Fry cashews and raisins in ghee; set aside. Temper bay leaves and whole spices with ginger.
Add rice and fry 3 minutes, then add 3 cups hot water and sugar; cover and cook on low heat until done, 15 minutes.
Fold in nuts and raisins and rest 5 minutes; serve with kosha mangsho or dhokar dalna.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 bay leaves, 3 cardamom, 3 cloves, 1 inch cinnamon
steps: Wash and drain the rice for 20 minutes.
Heat ghee, temper bay leaves and whole spices, and fry cashews and rice for 3 minutes.
Add 3 cups hot water, salt and sugar; cover and cook on low heat until fluffy.
Serve with mutton curry or deemer dalna.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Aloo bhaja or bhorta to serve
steps: Cover the cooked rice with water and leave covered overnight at room temperature to ferment lightly.
In the morning add salt, crushed chillies, onion and raw mustard oil.
Eat cool, with fried potatoes or mashed bhorta, on hot summer days and at Poila Boishakh.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg raw green mangoes, cut in small pieces
2 tbsp panch phoron, roasted and ground
steps: Toss mango with salt and turmeric and sun-dry 2–3 days until slightly shrivelled.
Heat the mustard oil to smoking and cool slightly.
Mix mango with panch phoron powder, chilli and sugar, pour over the oil and fill clean dry jars.
Sun the jars for a week; use the spiced oil over muri or rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1/2 tsp panch phoron, 1 dried red chilli
steps: Temper panch phoron and red chilli in mustard oil.
Add tomatoes, ginger and salt and cook until soft.
Add sugar, dates, raisins and aamsotto and simmer until glossy and jammy, about 15 minutes.
Cool and serve at the end of the meal.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 40 phuchka shells (made of atta and semolina)
1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1 tsp black salt
Tamarind water: 2 tbsp tamarind pulp, 4 cups water, gondhoraj lime, black salt, roasted cumin, mint
steps: Mash potato with chana, chillies, coriander, roasted cumin, black salt and salt into a spicy filling.
Mix the tamarind water with lime, black salt, cumin and mint and chill.
Crack each shell, stuff with filling, dip in tamarind water and eat at once.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Black salt, roasted cumin, lime juice
steps: Toss all the vegetables, peanuts and chanachur in a large bowl.
Add muri, mustard oil, black salt, roasted cumin and lime.
Toss quickly and serve at once in paper cones.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 cups dried yellow peas (motor), soaked overnight
1 tsp cumin powder, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp chilli
Bhaja masala (roasted cumin-chilli powder), onion, chilli, tamarind water to garnish
steps: Pressure-cook the peas with turmeric and salt until soft but whole.
Temper bay leaves, fry potato and onion, then add ginger, tomato and spices and cook until the oil separates.
Add peas with cooking water and simmer 15 minutes until thick, adding a pinch of sugar.
Serve topped with raw onion, chilli, bhaja masala and a splash of tamarind water.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Vegetables: onion rings, potato and pumpkin slices, brinjal slices, chillies
1/2 tsp kalo jeere, pinch of baking soda
steps: Whisk besan, rice flour, spices, kalo jeere, soda and salt with water into a thick batter.
Dip each vegetable and deep-fry in hot mustard oil until crisp and golden.
Serve with muri and tea on a rainy evening.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1/2 tsp kalo jeere, pinch of soda
steps: Make a smooth, thick batter of besan, rice flour, spices, kalo jeere, soda and salt.
Coat each brinjal slice and deep-fry until puffed and golden.
Serve with khichuri or muri.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Rub ghee into flour, add kalo jeere and salt and knead a stiff dough; rest 20 minutes.
Roll thin and cut into diamonds or fold into triangles.
Fry on low-medium heat until crisp and pale golden; cool and store airtight for Bijoya.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Dough: 2 cups maida, 4 tbsp ghee, salt, water
1 tsp roasted cumin powder, sugar, salt
steps: Knead a stiff dough with ghee and rest 30 minutes.
Temper panch phoron, fry potatoes, cauliflower, peas, peanuts, ginger and chillies with salt and sugar until cooked; add roasted cumin.
Shape dough into cones, fill and seal.
Fry on low heat until crisp and golden; serve with tomato chutney.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Boil milk, curdle with lime juice, strain the chhana in muslin and rinse; hang 30 minutes.
Knead the chhana with your palm 8–10 minutes until smooth and greasy; roll into 12 crack-free balls.
Boil sugar and water into a thin syrup, drop in the balls, cover and boil hard 15 minutes until doubled.
Cool in the syrup; add rose water and serve chilled.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp lime juice, diluted in 2 tbsp water
1/3 cup powdered sugar or grated nolen gur
steps: Boil the milk, lower the heat and add the lime water to curdle it; strain the chhana through muslin, rinse and hang 30 minutes.
Knead the chhana with the heel of your palm for 5 minutes until smooth.
Cook it with the sugar in a non-stick pan on low heat, stirring, for 6–8 minutes until it just leaves the sides (overcooking makes it grainy).
Cool until warm, knead in cardamom and press into moulds or shape by hand; top with pistachios and saffron.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1/2 cup sugar or crumbled nolen gur
3 tbsp thick plain yogurt as starter
steps: Boil the milk and reduce on medium heat, stirring, to about two-thirds.

2 green cardamoms, 1 bay leaf, 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste

steps: Heat ghee, add cardamom and bay leaf, then onion paste and ginger-garlic; cook 8 minutes without browning.
Add tomato purée and chilli and cook 10 minutes until the ghee separates.
Lower heat, stir in curd and nut paste and cook 5 minutes.
Add 1/2 cup water, salt, sugar and paneer and simmer 5 minutes.
Finish with cream, garam masala and kasuri methi; serve with naan.

ingredients: 1 onion and 2 spring onions, finely chopped
1 tbsp soy sauce, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 1 tsp salt
Red chutney: 4 tomatoes, 8 dried red chillies, 6 garlic cloves, vinegar, salt
steps: Knead maida with salt and water into a firm dough; rest 30 minutes.
Mix chicken with onion, spring onion, ginger-garlic, soy, pepper, salt and oil.
Roll small thin wrappers, fill and pleat into momos.
Steam on an oiled steamer 12–15 minutes until the filling is cooked through.
Blanch tomatoes, chillies and garlic and blend with vinegar and salt for the fiery red chutney; serve momos with chutney and mayonnaise, Delhi-style.

ingredients: 2 black tea bags, 1 black cardamom, 1 bay leaf
2 onions, finely chopped, and 3 tomatoes, puréed
1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and 2 green chillies
2 tbsp chole masala, 1 tsp amchur, 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli, salt
Bhature: 2 cups maida, 2 tbsp semolina, 1/2 cup curd, 1/4 tsp baking soda, 1 tsp sugar, salt
Oil for deep frying; onion rings, pickled carrot and green chilli to serve
steps: Knead the bhatura dough with curd, soda, sugar and salt into a soft dough; rub with oil and rest 2–3 hours.
Pressure-cook chickpeas with tea bags, cardamom, bay leaf and salt 5–6 whistles until very soft; discard tea bags.
Fry onions in ghee until deep brown, add ginger-garlic, chillies, tomato and spices and cook until oil separates.
Add chickpeas with their dark stock, mash a few, and simmer 20 minutes until thick.
Roll bhaturas into ovals and deep-fry in very hot oil, pressing so they balloon; serve with chole, onion and pickle, Sita Ram Diwan Chand-style.

ingredients: 4 aloo tikkis (potato, cornflour, salt, cumin, chilli, amchur)
1 onion, sliced into rings, and 1 tomato, sliced
steps: Shallow-fry the tikkis on a tawa in a little oil 6–8 minutes per side until crisp and golden.
Toast the buns cut-side down in butter on the tawa until golden.
Spread green chutney and saunth inside each bun.
Add a hot tikki, onion and tomato, sprinkle chaat masala and press shut; serve hot from the tawa.

ingredients: 1 kg mutton (shoulder and ribs), cut in large pieces
1 tbsp Kashmiri chilli powder (dissolved in 1/2 cup water)
4 green cardamom, 2 black cardamom, 4 cloves, 1 bay leaf
1 tbsp ratanjot (alkanet) infused in hot oil, for colour (optional)
steps: Heat mustard oil in a heavy pot until it smokes, cool slightly, then add whole spices and hing water.
Add mutton and salt and sear on high heat for 8–10 minutes until the pieces turn brown and the water dries.
Stir in the chilli-water and cook until the oil separates and turns red, about 3 minutes.
Add whisked curd a little at a time, stirring constantly so it does not split, then add saunf and sonth powder with 2 cups water.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 60–70 minutes until the meat is tender and a red film of oil (rogan) floats on top; add ratanjot oil if using.
Serve hot with steamed rice — the Kashmiri Pandit way, with no onion or garlic.

ingredients: 4 green cardamom, 2 black cardamom, 4 cloves, 1 cinnamon stick, 2 bay leaves
steps: Boil the mutton in 5 cups water with salt, black cardamom, cloves and cinnamon for 45 minutes until nearly tender; keep the stock.
Whisk curd with saunf and sonth and cook in a separate pot on low heat, stirring continuously, until it comes to a boil without splitting.
Add the mutton and 2 cups strained stock to the curd and simmer 15–20 minutes until the gravy is creamy.
Heat ghee, crackle green cardamom and shahi zeera, and pour over; finish with crushed dried mint.
Serve with plain steamed rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg boneless mutton leg with 200 g mutton fat
steps: Pound the meat and fat on a stone with a wooden mallet (or mince finely in a processor) with salt and cardamom powder until very smooth and sticky.
Wet your hands and shape into large balls the size of an orange, about 8–10.
Simmer the balls in 6 cups water with whole spices for 30 minutes until firm; reserve the stock.
Cook whisked curd with ghee, saunf and sonth on low heat, stirring constantly, until it boils; add 2 cups stock.
Add the balls and simmer 20 minutes until the gravy is creamy and glossy.
Finish with dried mint; traditionally served last at a Wazwan with rice.

ingredients: 1 kg boneless mutton with 200 g fat
1 tbsp ratanjot-infused oil or Kashmiri red colour
1 tbsp onion paste (fried) or Kashmiri ver masala
steps: Pound the meat and fat with salt and cardamom until smooth, then shape into medium meatballs about 4 cm wide.
Bring 6 cups water to a boil with the whole spices, add the balls and simmer 25 minutes.
Heat mustard oil to smoking, cool slightly, and add chilli powder dissolved in water, onion paste or ver, saunf and sonth.
Add the balls with 2 cups stock and the ratanjot oil and simmer 20 minutes until the gravy is bright red and oil floats on top.
Serve hot with rice.

ingredients: 1 kg lamb ribs (with fat), cut in rib pieces
steps: Place ribs in a wide pan with milk, 2 cups water, spices and salt.
Simmer on low heat for 50–60 minutes, turning occasionally, until the meat is tender and the liquid has fully evaporated.
Heat ghee in a frying pan and shallow-fry the ribs on medium heat for 4–5 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp.
Drain and serve hot as a starter with radish chutney (muj chetin).

ingredients: 600 g baby potatoes, boiled and peeled
steps: Prick the potatoes all over with a fork and deep- or shallow-fry in mustard oil on medium heat until golden, about 8 minutes.
In 2 tbsp of the oil, crackle whole spices and hing, then add chilli powder mixed with 1/4 cup water and cook 1 minute.
Lower the heat and add curd gradually, stirring constantly, then add saunf, sonth, salt and 1 cup water.
Add the fried potatoes, cover tightly and cook on dum (very low heat) for 15–20 minutes until the gravy is thick and red.
Serve with rice or roti.

ingredients: 500 g haak (Kashmiri collard greens), whole leaves washed
steps: Heat mustard oil to smoking point, cool slightly and add hing and dried chillies.
Add 2 cups water, salt and green chillies and bring to a boil.
Add the whole haak leaves (and soda if using) and simmer uncovered for 12–15 minutes until tender but still bright green.
Serve in its thin broth with steamed rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g nadru (lotus stem), peeled and sliced diagonally
steps: Blanch the lotus stem slices in boiling water for 3 minutes and drain well.
Whisk rice flour, besan, chilli, saunf, hing and salt with water into a thick batter.
Dip each slice in batter and deep-fry in hot mustard oil on medium heat for 3–4 minutes until crisp and golden.
Serve hot as a street snack with walnut and radish chutney.

ingredients: 400 g nadru (lotus stem), peeled and cut in 5 cm pieces
steps: Pressure-cook the lotus stem in 2 cups water with salt for 3 whistles until tender; reserve the water.
Heat ghee and crackle cardamom, cloves, bay leaf and shahi zeera.
Lower the heat and add curd with saunf and sonth, stirring continuously until it comes to a boil.
Add the lotus stem with 1 cup cooking water and simmer 10 minutes until the gravy is creamy.
Sprinkle dried mint and serve with rice.

ingredients: 1 cup milk with a pinch of saffron soaked in it
steps: Fry the nuts and raisins in 1 tbsp ghee until golden; set aside.
Heat remaining ghee, add whole spices, then add drained rice and fry gently for 2 minutes.
Add 1 1/2 cups water, saffron milk, sugar and salt; bring to a boil.
Cover and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes.
Fold in fried nuts and raisins; serve warm at weddings and festivals.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Boil water with cardamom and cinnamon for 5 minutes.
Add saffron and green tea, turn off the heat and steep 2 minutes.

ingredients: 2 tbsp Kashmiri green tea leaves (or gunpowder tea)
steps: Boil tea leaves, soda and 2 cups water for 15–20 minutes until reduced to a dark red concentrate.
Add 1 cup cold water and aerate by pouring from a height with a ladle for 3 minutes — this turns it pink.

ingredients: 4 kg mutton, divided for rista, rogan josh, tabak maaz, gushtaba and yakhni
1 cup mustard oil and 1 cup ghee
Whole spices: green and black cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaf
Walnut and radish chutney, and curd, to serve

steps: Boil the mutton in 4 cups water with salt, cloves and cinnamon for 45 minutes until tender.
In a separate pot, simmer the milk for 20 minutes, stirring, until reduced by a third.
Add the mutton and 1 cup stock to the milk with saunf, sonth and cardamom powder and simmer 15 minutes until creamy.
Temper shahi zeera in hot ghee and pour over; serve with rice.

ingredients: 2 tbsp Kashmiri chilli powder plus 6 dried red chillies, soaked and ground
1 tbsp Kashmiri ver masala (spice cake), crumbled
2 onions, sliced and fried crisp, ground to a paste
steps: Heat mustard oil to smoking, cool slightly, add whole spices and sear the mutton for 10 minutes until browned.
Add the red chilli paste and powder and fry 3 minutes until fragrant and deep red.
Add onion paste, saunf, sonth, salt and 2 cups water.
Cover and simmer 50–60 minutes until the meat is tender and the gravy is thick and fiery.

ingredients: 1 kg lamb ribs, in pairs of ribs
1/2 tsp saffron soaked in 2 tbsp milk
steps: Simmer ribs in milk and 2 cups water with whole spices, saunf and salt for 50 minutes until tender and the liquid has evaporated.
Cool slightly, then whisk curd, rice flour and saffron into a batter.

Shallow-fry in hot ghee for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and crisp; serve hot.

ingredients: 1 whole chicken (1.2 kg), cut in 4 large pieces
1/2 tsp saffron soaked in warm milk

Remove the chicken and reduce the stock by half.
Fry the chicken pieces in ghee for 5 minutes until golden.

ingredients: 500 g boneless mutton, cut in small cubes

steps: Heat ghee, add cardamom and cloves, then sear the mutton with salt for 10 minutes until browned.

Add the koftas and turnips and seal the lid with dough.

Open, add saffron and serve the next morning with rice or bread.

steps: Peel the kohlrabi bulbs and slice; wash and roughly tear the leaves.

steps: Fry the brinjal pieces in hot mustard oil until browned; set aside.

ingredients: 1 cup mixed fruit (apple, pineapple, pomegranate), diced
2 tbsp each cashews, almonds, walnuts, raisins
4 green cardamom, 4 cloves, 1 cinnamon stick, 1 bay leaf

steps: Mix yeast, sugar and warm water, rest 10 minutes, then knead with flour and salt into a soft dough.
Rise for 1–2 hours.

Serve with noon chai or wrap with butter.

Knead with flour, salt, cardamom and ghee into a soft dough; rise 1–2 hours.
Roll into thick rounds, prick with a fork and brush with saffron milk.
Bake at 220°C for 12–15 minutes until golden; brush with ghee and serve with kahwa.

Stir in rose water, pour into clay bowls (shikoras) and chill 2 hours; garnish with nuts.

ingredients: 1 cup mixed dry fruits (almonds, cashews, walnuts), chopped
100 g paneer, cubed and fried golden
steps: Lightly fry the nuts, coconut and paneer in ghee until golden; set aside.
Boil sugar with 1/2 cup water to a one-string syrup, about 6 minutes.
Add pepper, dry ginger and cardamom to the syrup.
Fold in the fried nuts, paneer and raisins and toss until coated; serve warm on festive days.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1/2 tsp saffron (kong) soaked in 2 tbsp warm milk
steps: Bring the milk to a boil and simmer 10 minutes.
Sprinkle in the semolina, stirring continuously, and cook on low heat 8 minutes until thickened.
Add sugar, saffron milk and cardamom and cook 3 more minutes.
Pour into bowls, chill and garnish with nuts.

steps: Rub ghee into flour, sugar, salt and baking powder until crumbly.
Add milk and knead lightly into a firm dough; rest 30 minutes.
Shape into small thick discs about 1 cm high and sprinkle poppy seeds on top.
Bake at 180°C for 20–25 minutes until crisp and pale golden; serve with noon chai.

ingredients: 1 cup Bhaderwah or Chinta rajma (small red beans), soaked overnight
steps: Pressure-cook the rajma with 1 tsp salt and 3 cups water for 6 whistles until soft and creamy.
Heat mustard oil, fry onion until golden, then add ginger, tomato and spice powders and cook 8 minutes until oil separates.
Add the rajma with its liquid and simmer 20 minutes, mashing a few beans to thicken.
Boil the rice in salted water until just tender and drain.
Serve the rajma over rice with a dollop of ghee and pickle — the classic Jammu Sunday lunch.

ingredients: 4 pieces kalari (Jammu ripened cheese), sliced thick
steps: Heat a dry non-stick pan and cook the kalari slices on medium heat for 2–3 minutes per side until golden and the inside turns gooey.
Toast the kulchas in butter on the same pan.
Place the hot kalari in the kulcha with onion, tomato, chilli, salt and chaat masala.
Serve immediately, the Udhampur street-food way.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tbsp tamarind pulp (or 2 tbsp dried anardana soaked)
steps: Heat mustard oil to smoking, cool slightly, and add methi seeds and hing.
Add the pumpkin, turmeric, chilli and salt and stir-fry 5 minutes.
Add 1 cup water, cover and cook 15 minutes until the pumpkin is soft.
Stir in tamarind and jaggery and simmer 10 minutes, mashing lightly, until thick, sweet and sour.

recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 tbsp dried pomegranate seeds (anardana), soaked and ground, or 3 tbsp lemon juice

Add mutton and ginger-garlic and sear on high heat for 10 minutes.
Add chilli, coriander, turmeric and salt and fry 3 minutes, then add 3 cups water.
Cover and simmer 50–60 minutes until the meat is tender.
Stir in the anardana paste or lemon juice and simmer 5 minutes until tangy; serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tsp yellow mustard seeds (rai), ground to a powder
1 cup diced cucumber or boiled pumpkin
steps: Mix the ground mustard with curd, salt and chilli powder.
Fold in the vegetables and green chilli, cover and leave at room temperature for 1–2 days until pungent and sour.
Drizzle with mustard oil and serve chilled as a tangy side to rice and rajma.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Pressure-cook the soaked kulth with turmeric, salt and 4 cups water for 8–10 whistles until soft.
Heat ghee, crackle cumin and hing, and fry onion until golden.
Add ginger, tomato and chilli powder and cook 5 minutes.
Add the dal and simmer 15 minutes, mashing lightly; serve hot with rice in winter.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 cup black chana or rongi (lobia), soaked overnight
steps: Pressure-cook the soaked pulses with salt and 3 cups water until soft.
Whisk curd with besan, turmeric and 1 cup water until smooth.
Heat mustard oil, crackle methi seeds and hing, then add chilli powder and the curd mixture, stirring constantly.
Add the cooked pulses and simmer 15–20 minutes until thick and tangy; serve with rice at a Dogra dham.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1/2 cup curd or a little leftover fermented dough
Mustard oil or ghee, for frying
steps: Mix flour, curd, sugar and salt with warm water into a soft batter-like dough and rest in a warm place 4–5 hours until it rises.
Wet your palms and flatten small portions into thick discs.
Deep-fry in hot oil on medium heat for 2–3 minutes per side until puffed and golden.
Serve with chana or kheer, as made for Dogra festivals.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1/2 cup jaggery powder or boora sugar
1/2 cup mixed almonds, cashews and walnuts, chopped
steps: Fry the gond in 2 tbsp ghee until puffed; crush. Roast the nuts and makhana in the same ghee.
Roast the flour in the remaining ghee on low heat for 15–20 minutes, stirring, until golden and nutty.
Turn off the heat and mix in sonth, coconut, gond and nuts.
Cool slightly, stir in jaggery and store in a jar; eaten in winter and given to new mothers.

steps: Knead the flour with water into a firm dough and rest 10 minutes.
Pinch off thumb-sized pieces and press each on your palm into a small cap-like shape.
Heat ghee, fry onion and tomato, then add vegetables, salt and 6 cups water and boil 10 minutes.
Drop in the dough caps and simmer 15 minutes until cooked through; add milk and greens for the last 5 minutes.
Serve hot in bowls as a hearty winter stew.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g mutton or chicken, thinly sliced
1 carrot and a handful of spinach
steps: Boil the meat in 6 cups water with salt for 25–30 minutes until tender and cooked through; keep the broth.
Heat oil, fry onion, ginger-garlic and chillies, then add tomatoes and cook until soft.
Pour in the broth and meat, add carrot and simmer 5 minutes.
Add noodles and spinach and cook 4–5 minutes until tender.
Serve steaming with spring onion and chilli sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Knead the flour into a firm dough, roll thin and cut into small squares; pinch each into a bow-tie shape.
Heat ghee, fry onion and garlic, then add tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add the potatoes, carrot, salt and 6 cups water and boil 10 minutes.
Drop in the pasta bows and simmer 10–12 minutes until cooked; add greens for the last 3 minutes.
Garnish with coriander and serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp dry yeast or a piece of sourdough starter
steps: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water, then knead with flour and salt into a soft dough.
Leave in a warm place for 3–4 hours until well risen.
Shape into thick round loaves about 3 cm high, scoring a ring or cross on top.
Cook in a covered heavy pan on low heat for 12–15 minutes per side (or bake at 200°C for 25 minutes) until brown and hollow-sounding.
Serve with butter tea and apricot jam.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tbsp brick tea or black tea leaves
steps: Boil the tea leaves (and soda) in water for 10 minutes until dark.
Strain into a tall wooden churn (gurgur) or a blender with milk, butter and salt.
Churn vigorously for 2 minutes until frothy and emulsified — the sound gives it its name.
Reheat gently and serve with tsampa or khambir.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Knead the flour with water and a pinch of salt into a firm dough; rest 20 minutes.
Mix the mince with onion, spring onion, ginger-garlic, oil, pepper, salt and coriander.
Roll small thin discs, fill with a spoon of the mixture and pleat into half-moons or rounds.
Steam on an oiled rack over boiling water for 15–18 minutes until the filling is cooked through.
Serve hot with tomato-chilli chutney and a bowl of the clear soup.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix yeast, sugar and warm water, rest 10 minutes, then knead with flour, salt and baking powder into a soft dough; rise 1–2 hours.
Roll into a thin sheet, brush with oil, roll into a log and cut into 5 cm pieces.
Stretch and twist each piece into a spiral bun.
Steam over boiling water for 15–18 minutes until fluffy; serve with dal, shapta or thukpa.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Bring water and salt to a boil in a heavy pot.
Add the mixed flours gradually, stirring hard with a wooden spoon to avoid lumps.

steps: Heat oil, fry onion and ginger-garlic, then add tomatoes and cook until soft.

Eat directly as a filling Ladakhi breakfast.

4 apricot kernels (sweet variety), blanched and slivered (optional)

Pour hot into sterilised jars, seal and serve with khambir and butter tea.

ingredients: 1 cup rajma, soaked overnight (for madra-style rajma)
2 tsp cumin, 1 tsp turmeric, 2 bay leaves
1 tbsp dham masala (cinnamon, clove, cardamom, black pepper), ground
1/2 cup jaggery, 1 tsp tamarind paste (for mittha and khatta)
steps: Boil the rice in plenty of water until just done and drain — dham rice is plain and fluffy, cooked by the botis (hereditary cooks) in large brass charoti pots.
Pressure-cook the rajma until tender, then simmer in a little ghee with cumin, turmeric, half the dham masala and 1 cup curd, stirring constantly, until thick (madra).
Cook the chana dal with turmeric and salt until soft but whole, then temper with ghee, cumin and bay leaves.
Make a quick khatta by simmering tamarind paste, jaggery, salt and a pinch of masala in 1 cup water for 10 minutes, and a mittha by cooking a cup of the rice with jaggery, raisins and dates in ghee.
Serve everything in sequence on pattal (leaf plates), guests seated on the floor — rice first, then dal, madra, khatta and mittha last.

ingredients: 1/2 cup poppy seeds (khus khus), soaked and ground
2 green chillies, 1 inch ginger, small bunch coriander, chopped
steps: Knead the flour, yeast, sugar, salt and warm water into a soft dough; cover and rest in a warm place 2–3 hours until doubled.
Mix walnuts, poppy paste, chillies, ginger, coriander and salt into a thick filling.
Roll palm-sized ovals, place a spoonful of filling, fold over and seal the edges.
Steam on a greased plate for 20–25 minutes until the siddu springs back when pressed.
Serve hot, split open and drenched in ghee, with green chutney or dal — the Kullu-Shimla winter favourite.

ingredients: 1.5 cups white chickpeas (kabuli chana), soaked overnight
1 tsp cumin seeds, 2 bay leaves, 4 cloves, 2 black cardamom
1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1/2 tsp red chilli powder
steps: Pressure-cook the chickpeas with salt for 4–5 whistles until tender; drain and keep the water.
Whisk the curd with besan, turmeric, coriander and chilli powder so it will not split.
Heat ghee, crackle cumin, bay leaves, cloves, cardamom and cinnamon, then add the chickpeas and fry 3 minutes.
Lower the heat and pour in the curd, stirring continuously in one direction until it comes to a boil.
Simmer 20–25 minutes, adding chickpea water if needed, until thick and the ghee surfaces; add raisins and serve with dham rice.

ingredients: 750 g lamb or mutton, curry cut
1 tsp turmeric, 1.5 tsp red chilli powder, 2 tsp coriander powder
steps: Marinate the lamb with ginger-garlic, turmeric, chilli and salt for 1–2 hours.
Heat mustard oil to smoking, cool slightly, then fry the whole spices and onions until golden.
Add the lamb and bhuno on medium heat for 15 minutes until browned; add 1 cup water and cook covered (or pressure-cook 4 whistles) until tender.
Whisk besan into the buttermilk with coriander powder until lump-free, then pour into the pot on low heat, stirring constantly.
Simmer 15 minutes until the gravy is thick and silky; finish with garam masala and serve with steamed rice.

ingredients: 1 cup black gram (kale chane) or urad dal, soaked overnight
1 tsp ajwain, 1/2 tsp red chilli powder
Mustard oil or refined oil for deep-frying
steps: Knead flour, yeast, sugar, salt and water into a soft dough; rest 2 hours.
Grind the soaked dal coarsely with ginger, chillies, ajwain, chilli powder and salt into a thick paste.
Flatten a ball of dough, place a spoon of filling, seal and gently roll into a 12 cm disc.
Deep-fry in hot oil over medium flame until puffed and golden on both sides, about 3 minutes each.
Serve hot with imli (tamarind) chutney or chana — the Himachali kachori.

1 pinch saffron in 2 tbsp warm milk
steps: Boil the rice in plenty of water until 80% done and drain.
Heat ghee, fry cardamom, cloves, cashews, raisins, dates and coconut until golden.
Add sugar with 1/4 cup water and stir until it melts into a syrup.
Fold in the rice and saffron milk, cover and cook on the lowest heat 10–12 minutes until the syrup is absorbed.
Serve warm as the closing sweet of a dham.

ingredients: 1/2 cup masoor or arhar dal, soaked 1 hour
1 tsp cumin, 2 bay leaves, 2 black cardamom, 4 cloves, 1 inch cinnamon
1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder
steps: Heat mustard oil to smoking, cool slightly and crackle cumin and whole spices; fry onions until brown.
Add ginger-garlic, tomatoes and powdered spices and cook until oil separates; stir in curd and cook 3 minutes.
Add potatoes and dal and fry 5 minutes, then add the drained rice and 3 cups hot water with salt.
Cover and cook on low heat 20 minutes until the rice and dal are soft and the water absorbed.

ingredients: 2 cups buckwheat or spinach leaves, finely chopped
steps: Whisk the flours, soda, salt and water into a thick pouring batter and rest 15 minutes.
Stir in the chopped leaves.
Pour a ladle onto a greased tawa, spread thick and cook on low heat with ghee, about 4 minutes per side, until set and browned.
Serve hot with ghee or curd — the Lahaul-Spiti buckwheat cake made at the Phagli festival.

ingredients: 2 whole rainbow trout (about 300 g each), cleaned and scored
1/2 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp red chilli powder
steps: Rub the trout inside and out with lemon juice, salt, turmeric, chilli and ginger-garlic; rest 20 minutes.
Heat mustard oil in a wide pan until hot, then lay the fish in.
Pan-fry on medium heat 5–6 minutes per side until the skin is crisp and the flesh flakes and is opaque to the bone.
Garnish with coriander and serve with boiled potatoes or rice — Beas river trout kept simple.

1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1/2 tsp turmeric
steps: Mix besan, tamarind, spices, ajwain and salt with water into a thick spreadable paste.

Shallow-fry slices in mustard oil until crisp on both sides and serve with chutney.

steps: Grind the dal to a thick, fluffy batter with hing and salt; steam it in a greased tray 20 minutes and cut into cubes (sepu vadi).
Shallow-fry the vadi cubes in mustard oil until golden and keep aside.
In the same oil crackle cumin, then fry onions, ginger-garlic and tomatoes with the powdered spices until oil separates.

steps: Dry-roast the bhatt in an iron kadhai on medium heat 8–10 minutes until they crackle and the skins split.

ingredients: 500 g young stinging nettle tops (kandalee / bichhu ghas), picked with gloves

steps: Soak the jhangora 15 minutes and drain.

steps: Knead the flours, salt and warm water into a soft dough, kneading well since mandua has little gluten.

Cook on a hot tawa 2 minutes per side, then puff briefly over the flame.

steps: Drain the rice, spread on a cloth to dry 1 hour, then grind to a slightly coarse damp flour.

ingredients: 1/2 cup gahat, 1/4 cup kala bhatt, 1/4 cup rajma, soaked overnight
1 tsp jakhiya or cumin, 1/2 tsp asafoetida
steps: Cook the soaked pulses in 6 cups water with turmeric and salt until soft, about 45 minutes; strain and keep the broth (the pulses can be used separately).
Heat ghee, crackle jakhiya, hing and chillies, then stir in rice flour and coriander powder for 1 minute.
Pour in the broth, whisking, and simmer 10 minutes until lightly thickened.
Garnish with coriander and serve hot as a soup or with rice.

ingredients: 1 cup arhar or gahat dal, soaked overnight
1 tbsp rice, soaked with the dal
1 inch ginger, 4 garlic cloves, 2 green chillies
1 tsp jakhiya or cumin, 1/2 tsp asafoetida
1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp red chilli powder
steps: Grind the dal and rice with ginger, garlic and chillies to a smooth thick paste.
Heat oil in an iron kadhai, crackle jakhiya and hing, add the spices and the paste, and roast 5 minutes on low heat.
Add 4 cups water and salt, whisking out lumps, and simmer 25–30 minutes, stirring, until thick and smooth.
Serve with steamed rice — a Kumaoni comfort dal.

ingredients: 1/2 cup bhang ke beej (hemp seeds — the non-intoxicating seeds sold in pahadi markets)
2 tbsp lemon juice (or hill lemon / galgal juice)
steps: Dry-roast the hemp seeds and cumin in a pan 3–4 minutes until they crackle and smell nutty.
Grind them with chillies, mint, salt and a little water into a coarse paste.
Stir in lemon juice and serve with aloo ke gutke, mandua roti or pakoras.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g tender stinging nettle tops (sisunak), picked with gloves
1 tsp jakhiya or cumin, 1/2 tsp asafoetida
steps: Wearing gloves, boil the nettles 10 minutes to remove the sting; drain and chop or grind coarsely.
Heat mustard oil, crackle jakhiya, red chillies, hing and garlic.
Add the nettles, turmeric, coriander and salt and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in the rice flour mixed with 1 cup water and simmer 10 minutes until thick; serve with mandua roti and ghee — the Kumaoni way.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Bring the water and salt to a rolling boil in a heavy pan.
Add the mandua flour in a steady stream while stirring vigorously with a wooden spoon to avoid lumps.
Cook on low heat 10–15 minutes, pressing and turning, until it forms a thick, smooth mass that leaves the pan.
Shape into balls with wet hands, top with ghee and serve with gahat dal or phaanu.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder
1 tsp jakhiya or cumin, 1/2 tsp fenugreek seeds, 2 dry red chillies
steps: Whisk curd, besan, water, turmeric and salt until lump-free.
Heat mustard oil, crackle jakhiya, fenugreek, red chillies and hing.
Pour in the curd mixture and bring to a boil, stirring continuously.
Simmer 25 minutes on low heat until thick and tangy, add chilli powder and serve with rice — the Kumaoni kadhi.

ingredients: 2 bay leaves, 2 black cardamom, 4 cloves, 1 tsp jakhiya or cumin
1 tsp turmeric, 2 tsp red chilli powder, 2 tsp coriander powder
steps: Marinate the mutton with curd, ginger-garlic, turmeric and salt for 2 hours.
Heat mustard oil to smoking, cool slightly, crackle jakhiya and whole spices, and fry the onions until dark brown.
Add the mutton and bhuno on high heat 15 minutes, then add tomatoes and powdered spices and cook until oil separates.
Add 2 cups hot water, cover and cook on low heat 60 minutes (or pressure-cook 6 whistles) until the mutton is fully tender.
Finish with garam masala and serve with rice or mandua roti.

ingredients: 500 g mutton mince, fatty, minced twice very fine
3 tbsp raw papaya paste (kachcha papita), as tenderiser
2 tbsp roasted chana dal flour (or besan)
1 tsp galouti masala (cardamom, mace, nutmeg, cinnamon, clove, rose petals, kebab chini)
1/2 tsp saffron in 1 tbsp kewra water
1 tsp salt, 1 tsp red chilli powder
steps: Grind the mince with papaya paste, fried onions, ginger-garlic, chana flour, spices, saffron-kewra and salt into a silky paste.
Cover and chill for 3–4 hours so the papaya softens the meat; optionally smoke it 5 minutes with a live coal and ghee (dhungar).
With wet hands shape small thin patties; they will be very soft.
Shallow-fry in ghee on a medium-hot tawa about 3 minutes per side until deep brown and cooked through (no pink inside).
Serve hot with ulte tawe ka paratha, onion rings and mint chutney.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g buffalo or mutton mince, minced very fine
1 tsp Tunday-style spice mix (cardamom, mace, nutmeg, cinnamon, clove, shahi jeera, rose petals)
1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp salt
steps: Pound or grind the mince with all ingredients except ghee to a smooth, sticky paste.
Rest covered in the fridge 3–4 hours.
Heat a large tawa with ghee on medium; drop small flat rounds and fry 3–4 minutes per side until crusted and fully cooked.
Serve straight from the tawa with ulte tawe ka paratha and sliced onions, the Aminabad way.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g mutton mince (raan) with 50 g kidney fat, minced fine
1/2 tsp each ground mace, green cardamom and cinnamon, pinch of clove
steps: Grind mince with fat, papaya, onion, chana powder, ginger-garlic, spices, saffron and salt to a fine paste.
Chill 3–4 hours until firm enough to hold on skewers.
Wrap the paste around flat seekh skewers with wet hands into long cylinders.
Grill over charcoal or under a hot grill, turning and basting with ghee, 8–10 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Slide off and serve with sheermal, onion rings and lemon.

ingredients: 6 dry red chillies, 1 tsp shahi jeera, 4 cloves, 2 black cardamoms, 1 inch cinnamon, 8 peppercorns
Filling: 1 small onion, 2 green chillies, mint and coriander, finely chopped
steps: Cook mutton with chana dal, whole spices, ginger, garlic, salt and 2 cups water until meat is very tender and dry, about 45 minutes (or 5 whistles in a pressure cooker).
Grind the mixture to a smooth dough, then knead in the egg.
Shape into patties, tucking a pinch of onion-mint filling into each centre.
Shallow-fry in ghee on medium heat, 2–3 minutes per side, until crisp and golden.
Serve with green chutney and sliced onions.

ingredients: 750 g boneless mutton leg, 1.5 inch cubes
1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1/2 tsp ground mace and cardamom
steps: Rub mutton with papaya, ginger-garlic and salt; rest 1 hour.
Add curd, onion paste, spices and lemon; marinate overnight in the fridge.
Skewer and grill over charcoal or at 240°C for 15–20 minutes, basting with ghee, until charred and tender with no pink juices.
Serve with mint chutney, onion rings and sheermal.

ingredients: Whole spices: 4 green cardamoms, 2 black cardamoms, 6 cloves, 2 bay leaves, cinnamon, shahi jeera, mace
1/2 tsp saffron in 1/4 cup warm milk
1 tbsp kewra water, 1 tsp rose water
steps: Make a yakhni: simmer mutton with whole spices, ginger-garlic, salt and 6 cups water about 1 hour until tender; strain and reserve the stock.
Brown the mutton in ghee, add curd and half the birista, cook 10 minutes on medium.
Parboil rice in the yakhni until 70% done; drain.
Layer the mutton and rice in a heavy handi; top with saffron milk, kewra, rose water, ghee and remaining birista.
Seal the lid with dough and cook on dum, very low heat, 30 minutes; rest 10 minutes.
Serve gently mixed, with burani raita and salan or korma — this pakki-style biryani is milder and more fragrant than Hyderabadi.

ingredients: 3 onions, sliced and fried brown, ground to paste
Whole spices: green cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaf
1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1/2 tsp mace-cardamom powder
Pinch of saffron, 1 tsp kewra water
steps: Marinate mutton with curd, ginger-garlic and salt for 45 minutes.
Crackle whole spices in ghee, add the mutton and sear on high 10 minutes.
Add chilli, coriander and fried onion paste; cook until ghee separates.
Add 2 cups hot water, cover and simmer on low about 60 minutes until meat is tender.
Stir in nut paste, mace-cardamom, saffron and kewra; simmer 10 minutes and serve with sheermal or warqi paratha.

ingredients: 1 kg mutton shanks (nalli) and boneless shoulder
4 tbsp wheat flour (atta), roasted in ghee
2 tbsp nihari masala (fennel, dry ginger, long pepper, mace, nutmeg, cardamom, clove, cinnamon, kebab chini)
To serve: Lucknowi kulcha, ginger juliennes, green chillies, lemon, coriander
steps: Sear meat and bones in ghee with ginger-garlic, chilli and half the nihari masala.
Add 10 cups water and salt; simmer covered on the lowest heat 5–6 hours (traditionally overnight) until meat falls off the bone.
Whisk the roasted atta into a cup of stock and stir back in; simmer 20 minutes until silky and thick.
Fry the onions and remaining masala in ghee and pour over as tadka.
Serve with warm kulcha, ginger, chillies and lemon — a Lucknow breakfast.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 750 g boneless mutton leg, cut into thin escalopes and flattened with a mallet
1 tsp red chilli powder, 1/2 tsp mace-cardamom powder
steps: Marinate pasande with papaya, curd, ginger-garlic, chilli and salt for 3–4 hours.
Sear the slices in hot ghee in batches until lightly browned.
Return all meat with the marinade and fried onion paste; add 1 cup water, cover and simmer on low 40 minutes until tender.
Stir in almond paste, mace-cardamom and cream; simmer 5 minutes until the gravy coats the meat. Serve with sheermal.

ingredients: Whole spices: cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaf
1 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder
Pinch of saffron, 1 tsp kewra water
steps: Marinate chicken in curd, ginger-garlic and salt for 30–60 minutes.
Fry whole spices in ghee, add chicken and sear on high 5 minutes.
Add chilli, coriander and fried onion paste; cook until oil separates.
Add 1 cup water, cover and simmer 20–25 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Stir in nut paste, saffron and kewra; simmer 5 minutes and serve with naan or sheermal.

ingredients: Whole spices: green and black cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, mace, bay leaf
1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder
Pinch of saffron, 1 tsp kewra water
Wheat dough, to seal the lid
steps: Mix mutton with curd, ginger-garlic, crushed fried onions, ground spices and salt; marinate 1 hour.
Put ghee and whole spices in a heavy handi, add the meat and stir on medium 10 minutes.
Sprinkle saffron and kewra, cover and seal the lid with dough.
Cook on the lowest heat (on a tawa) for 1.5 hours so the meat cooks in its own juices.
Break the seal at the table and serve with sheermal or warqi paratha.

ingredients: 2 tbsp almond paste, 1 tbsp melon seed (magaz) paste
1 tsp red chilli powder, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp mace-cardamom powder
steps: Brown the mutton in ghee with ginger-garlic, then add curd, fried onion paste, chilli, turmeric and salt.
Cook on medium until oil separates; add 2 cups hot water, cover and simmer 60 minutes until tender.
Stir in almond and magaz paste, saffron and mace-cardamom; simmer 10 minutes to a rich golden gravy.
Lay gold varq ("kundan") over the top just before serving with sheermal.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder
Whole spices: cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaf
1/2 tsp saffron in warm milk, 1 tsp kewra water
steps: Temper whole spices in ghee; add mutton and ginger-garlic and sear 10 minutes on high.
Add turmeric, chilli, salt and curd; cook until the curd dries and ghee rises.
Add crushed fried onions and 2 cups water; cover and simmer about 60 minutes until tender.
Finish with cashew paste, saffron milk and kewra; simmer 5 minutes. Serve with warqi paratha.

ingredients: 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder
Whole spices: black cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaf, peppercorns
To serve: ginger juliennes, lemon, coriander
steps: Blanch the trotters in boiling water 5 minutes; drain and rinse.
Fry whole spices, ginger-garlic, ground spices and half the fried onions in ghee; add trotters and roast 10 minutes.
Add 10 cups water and salt; simmer covered on low 4–5 hours (or 45 minutes in a pressure cooker) until the meat falls off the bone and the broth is gelatinous.
Finish with garam masala and remaining fried onions; serve hot with ginger, lemon and kulcha or sheermal.

ingredients: 1/2 tsp saffron in 3 tbsp warm milk
1/2 tsp cardamom powder, 1 tsp kewra water
steps: Knead maida, yeast, sugar, salt, cardamom, ghee, milk and kewra into a soft dough; rest 1 hour until risen.
Divide into 6, roll into 6-inch discs and dock all over with a fork.
Bake at 230°C for 6 minutes (traditionally in a tandoor).
Brush generously with saffron milk and bake 3–4 minutes more until glossy and golden.
Brush with ghee and serve warm with kebabs, nihari or korma.

ingredients: 3 tbsp ghee, plus extra for cooking
steps: Knead maida, milk, ghee, sugar, salt, cardamom and kewra into a soft dough; rest 30 minutes.
Roll each ball very thin, brush with ghee, pleat and coil, then roll out into a large thin disc.
Cook on an upturned kadhai (ulta tawa) over high heat, brushing with ghee and turning, until spotted golden, about 2 minutes.
Fold in quarters and serve with galouti or tunday kebab.

ingredients: Pinch of saffron in 1 tbsp milk
steps: Knead maida, sugar, salt, 2 tbsp ghee and milk into a soft dough; rest 30 minutes.
Roll thin, spread ghee, dust with flour, fold into a square; repeat roll-ghee-fold twice more to build leaves (warq).
Roll gently into a 6-inch square without pressing out the layers.
Cook on a medium-hot tawa with ghee, 2–3 minutes per side, until flaky and golden; brush with saffron milk.
Serve with korma or kaliya.

ingredients: 1/2 tsp baking powder, pinch of soda
steps: Knead maida, curd, milk, sugar, baking powder, soda, salt and 2 tbsp ghee into a soft dough; rest 2 hours.
Shape into rounds, press kalonji on top and pat into thick discs.
Bake in a tandoor, or at 240°C for 8–10 minutes, until puffed with brown spots.
Brush with ghee and serve with nihari.

ingredients: 1/2 tsp saffron in 1/4 cup warm milk
1/4 cup almonds and pistachios, slivered; 2 tbsp raisins
steps: Boil rice with a pinch of saffron until 80% cooked; drain.
Heat ghee with cardamom and cloves; add rice, sugar, saffron milk and kewra and fold gently.
Cover tightly and cook on dum, lowest heat, 20 minutes until the syrup is absorbed.
Top with nuts, raisins and khoya; serve warm.

ingredients: 6 slices white bread, crusts removed, halved
1/2 cup sugar syrup with 1/2 tsp cardamom
2 tbsp sliced almonds and pistachios, silver varq
steps: Simmer milk, stirring, about 40 minutes until reduced to a thick rabri; add sugar, saffron and kewra.
Fry bread in ghee on medium until crisp and golden.
Dip each piece briefly in warm cardamom syrup and arrange on a platter.
Pour rabri over, garnish with nuts and varq; serve warm or chilled.

ingredients: Pinch of saffron in 1 tbsp milk
steps: Heat milk and cream until just warm, then chill overnight in a wide pan (traditionally left out under winter dew).
Whisk the cold milk vigorously with sugar and cardamom (or use a hand blender) to raise a light foam.
Skim the foam into cups as it forms; drizzle saffron milk on top.
Garnish with pistachios and serve immediately — Lucknow's winter-morning "nimish".

steps: Simmer milk in a wide pan on low heat; collect the skin (malai) that forms every few minutes onto a plate, building thin sheets over about 1.5 hours.
Mix khoya, sugar, cardamom, nuts and saffron as the filling.
Cut the chilled malai sheets into squares, place filling in the centre and fold into triangles like a paan gilori.
Top with silver varq and serve chilled.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: To serve: falooda (cornflour noodles), rose syrup
steps: Simmer milk, stirring and scraping, about 60 minutes until reduced to a third.
Add sugar, khoya, saffron, cardamom, kewra and pistachios; cook 5 minutes and cool.
Pour into matka or kulfi moulds, seal and freeze overnight.
Unmould and serve sliced over falooda with rose syrup.

ingredients: 1/4 cup basmati rice, soaked and coarsely ground
steps: Bring milk to a boil, stir in ground rice and cook on low 20 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy.
Add sugar, cardamom and saffron; cook 5 minutes more and stir in kewra.
Pour into earthen saucers (shikoras) and chill 2 hours until set.
Garnish with nuts and serve cold.

ingredients: 1/2 tsp saffron in 2 tbsp warm milk
steps: Roast vermicelli in ghee on low heat until deep golden.
Make a light syrup of sugar and water; add saffron milk and cardamom.
Pour syrup over vermicelli, cover and cook on low 8–10 minutes until absorbed and the strands are separate.
Fold in khoya and nuts; serve warm.

ingredients: 1 cup cauliflower florets, 1/2 cup green peas
1 tsp cumin, 2 bay leaves, 4 cloves, 2 cardamoms
1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp garam masala
steps: Heat oil until smoking, then temper cumin and whole spices; fry onion golden.
Add ginger-garlic, turmeric, chilli and vegetables; sauté 5 minutes.
Add rice, salt and 3 cups water; bring to a boil, cover and cook on low 15 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes, fluff, sprinkle garam masala and coriander; serve with curd and papad.

ingredients: 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp garam masala
Tadka: 2 tbsp ghee, 4 garlic cloves sliced, 1 tsp cumin, 2 dry red chillies
steps: Fry onions in ghee until golden; add ginger-garlic, mutton and spices and roast 10 minutes.
Add tomatoes and cook until soft; add 3 cups water, cover and simmer 45 minutes until mutton is nearly tender.
Add dal and 2 cups water; simmer 30 minutes until dal is soft and meat fully tender.
Pour over a sizzling garlic-cumin-chilli tadka, garnish with coriander and serve with rice or roti.

ingredients: 2 large potatoes, grated and squeezed dry (for katoris)
1/2 cup boiled chickpeas and 1/2 cup boiled potato cubes
1 cup aloo tikki or papdi pieces
4 tbsp tamarind-date chutney, 4 tbsp green chutney
1 tsp chaat masala, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1/2 tsp red chilli powder
1/4 cup pomegranate seeds, fine sev, coriander
steps: Press grated potato into a basket ladle (or between two strainers) and deep-fry until crisp, making 4 katoris.
Fill each basket with chickpeas, potato, tikki or papdi.
Spoon over curd, both chutneys and the spice powders.
Top with pomegranate, sev and coriander and serve at once — the Royal Cafe, Hazratganj classic.

ingredients: 1.5 cups dried white peas (safed matar), soaked overnight
1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1 tsp chaat masala, 1/2 tsp black salt
1 inch ginger, julienned; 2 green chillies, chopped
steps: Pressure-cook peas with turmeric and salt until soft but holding shape (about 4 whistles), or simmer in a big pot as street vendors do.
Lightly mash a ladleful to thicken.
Serve hot in leaf bowls topped with onion, tomato, ginger, chillies, spice powders, tamarind chutney, lemon and coriander.

ingredients: 2 cups maida or wheat flour, 3 tbsp ghee (moyan), salt
1/2 cup urad dal, soaked 3 hours and coarsely ground
1 tsp saunf, 1 tsp dhaniya, 1/2 tsp hing, 1 tsp red chilli, ginger
4 potatoes, boiled and broken by hand
1 tsp panch phoron or jeera, 1/2 tsp methi seeds
1 tsp amchur, 1/2 tsp garam masala, salt, coriander
Mustard oil or ghee for frying
steps: Rub ghee into flour with salt, knead a firm dough and rest 30 minutes.
Fry the ground urad dal with hing, saunf, dhaniya, chilli and ginger in a little ghee on low heat 8–10 minutes until dry and aromatic; cool.
Stuff small balls of dough with the dal filling, flatten into kachoris and deep-fry on medium-low heat until crisp and golden, 6–8 minutes.

For the Banarasi aloo sabzi, crackle jeera and methi in oil, add tomatoes, chilli and turmeric, cook soft, then add broken potatoes and 3 cups water; simmer 15 minutes until thin and tangy, finish with amchur and garam masala.
Serve hot kachoris with the aloo sabzi and jalebi, as on the ghats of Varanasi.

ingredients: 1 tsp chaat masala, 1/2 tsp roasted jeera powder, 1/2 tsp black salt
2 tbsp sugar syrup and imli chutney
steps: Heat ghee in an iron kadhai on medium, add jeera, hing, ginger and chillies.
Add tomatoes and mashed potato and cook, mashing with a flat ladle, 15 minutes until thick and saucy.
Season with salt, chaat masala and roasted jeera; stir in a little sugar syrup.
Serve in kulhads topped with imli chutney, crushed namak pare and coriander — the Kashi Chaat Bhandar style.

ingredients: 4 Maghai or Banarasi paan leaves, washed
1/2 tsp chuna (slaked lime) paste, used sparingly
1 tbsp sweet saunf and dhaniya dal
steps: Trim the stems and thin veins of each leaf.
Smear a thin layer of kattha and the barest trace of chuna on the leaf.
Add gulkand, saunf, coconut and crushed cardamom (this sweet meetha paan has no tobacco).
Fold into a triangular gilori and pin with a clove; serve after a meal.

steps: Boil milk with sugar until slightly reduced, 15 minutes; cool and stir in milk powder.
Traditionally the milk is left outdoors on a winter night to catch the dew; at home chill it overnight in a wide pan.
At dawn, whisk vigorously (or use a hand blender) to lift a thick, airy foam; skim the foam into kulhads.
Drizzle saffron milk, sprinkle cardamom and pistachios and serve immediately — a Banarasi winter-morning treat.

ingredients: 1/2 cup urad dal, soaked 3 hours and ground coarse
1 tsp saunf, 1 tsp dhaniya, 1/2 tsp hing, 1 tsp red chilli, ginger
1 tsp amchur, 1 tsp kasuri methi, salt
steps: Mix flour, semolina, ground dal, spices and salt; knead a stiff dough and rest 20 minutes.
Roll small thick puris and deep-fry in hot oil until puffed and crisp.
For the aloo, temper methi and jeera, cook tomatoes with chilli and turmeric, add potatoes and water; simmer 15 minutes until runny.
Finish with amchur and kasuri methi; serve bedmi with the thin aloo and green chilli pickle — a Braj and Agra breakfast.

ingredients: 1 kg ash gourd (petha/safed kaddu), peeled and cubed
1 tbsp edible chuna (lime) dissolved in 2 litres water
1/2 tsp cardamom powder or a few drops kewra water
steps: Prick the ash gourd cubes all over with a fork and soak in the limewater overnight to firm them.
Rinse thoroughly in several changes of water; boil the cubes 10 minutes until translucent at the edges; drain.
Make a one-thread sugar syrup, add the gourd and simmer 30–40 minutes until fully glassy.
Add kewra or cardamom, cool in the syrup, then lift out and dry on a rack until the surface is crisp with sugar.

steps: Roast khoya with ghee in a heavy kadhai on low heat, stirring constantly, 30–35 minutes until deep brown and grainy (the Mathura colour).
Cool until warm, then mix in half the bura and the cardamom.
Shape into small rounds and roll in the remaining bura.
Offer as prasad or store airtight up to a week.

ingredients: 2 cups wheat flour, 2 tbsp ghee, salt, ajwain
1 onion, ginger, garlic, 2 green chillies, coriander, finely chopped
1 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tbsp mustard oil, 1 tsp achar masala
steps: Knead flour, ghee, ajwain and salt into a firm dough; mix sattu with onion, ginger, garlic, chilli, coriander, lemon, mustard oil and achar masala.
Stuff balls of dough with sattu, seal and roast over cow-dung cakes, coals or in a 200°C oven 30–40 minutes, turning, until cracked and cooked through.
Char brinjal and tomatoes over flame, boil potatoes; peel and mash all with mustard oil, garlic, chilli, onion and salt for the chokha.
Crack the batis, dunk in hot ghee and serve with chokha — a Purvanchal staple.

ingredients: 500 g baby potatoes, boiled and peeled
1 tsp Kashmiri chilli, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1/2 tsp garam masala
steps: Prick potatoes and fry in ghee until golden; set aside.
In the same ghee add hing, ginger and chillies, then tomato purée and powdered spices; cook until ghee separates, 8 minutes.
Lower the heat, add curd and cashew paste, stirring constantly so it does not split.
Add potatoes with 1/2 cup water, cover tightly and cook on dum 15 minutes; finish with garam masala and coriander and serve with puri.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 cups fresh green peas, coarsely ground
1 tbsp ginger, 4 garlic, 2 green chillies, ground
1 tsp jeera, 1 bay leaf, 1/4 tsp hing
1 tsp coriander powder, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp garam masala
steps: Heat mustard oil to smoking, cool slightly and fry potatoes and badi; remove.
